title: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro Ranks 4th on Artificial Analysis Index, Tops Open Models
summary:
Independent evaluator Artificial Analysis ranked Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro fourth overall on its Intelligence Index with a score of 55, up 11 points from Kimi K3's 44 and trailing only Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 58, Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 56 and Muse Wonder Full at 56. Once Moonshot publishes the model's weights by Nov. 4, K3.1 Pro will become the highest-scoring open-weight model on the index and cut the gap between the leading open-weight and proprietary models from 12 points to three.

In Artificial Analysis's independent tests, the 2.8T parameter model scored 67% on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 coding evaluation, up from 13% for Kimi K3 and the highest score of any model the firm has tested. It also placed third on GDPval-AA with a 1,846 Elo rating and rose from 58% to 73% on the AutomationBench-AA agentic workflow test. On Code Arena's WebDev leaderboard, K3.1 Pro ranked eighth with 1,692 points, matching Claude Opus 5 at a 74% lower median cost of $1.23 per task. Moonshot priced the API at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, a 33% reduction from K3 and half the token rate of Claude Opus 5.5.

Moonshot removed cybersecurity data from mid-training and reinforcement learning before release after an unfiltered checkpoint solved 90.5% of its internal software vulnerability exploitation tasks. The filtered model still solved 81% of those tasks, up from 33.3% for K3, and posted 95% on Artificial Analysis's CyberGym-E2E-AA benchmark, the highest score of any model tested by the evaluator. Moonshot stated that it held K3.1 Pro's offensive cyber performance below its internal pipeline and proprietary frontier models while planning to gradually raise open-weight cyber capabilities in future releases for defensive code auditing.

selectedTweets.text:
Kimi K3.1 Pro launches at 4th on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index scoring 55, making large gains in agentic performance; it will be the leading open-weights model once its weights are published

@Kimi_Moonshot's new reasoning model gains 11 points over Kimi K3 (max, 44). It trails only Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback, 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback, 56), and Muse Wonder Full (max, 56) on the Intelligence Index.

Once the weights for K3.1 Pro are released it will be the highest-scoring open weights model and the gap between the leading open weights and proprietary models on the Intelligence Index will narrow from 12 points to 3.

Key results:
➤ Large gains in agentic performance: Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 3rd on GDPval-AA with 1,846 Elo, up 312 Elo from Kimi K3, behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (1,866 Elo) and Muse Wonder Full (1,857 Elo). Kimi K3.1 Pro also achieves the highest score of any model on Terminal-Bench 4.0. K3.1 Pro scores 67%, up from 13% for Kimi K3 and ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (64%). AutomationBench-AA, which tests agentic SaaS workflows, rises from 58% to 73%.

➤ Gains in other evals are more moderate: Humanity's Last Exam rises from 47% to 52%, CritPt from 23% to 25%, and SciCode from 59% to 61%. AA-Omniscience Index rises from 20 to 30, as the hallucination rate falls from 53% to 44% and accuracy rises from 48% to 51%.

➤ Cost per Task roughly equal to Kimi K3 at $1.98 per Task: K3.1 Pro uses 55K output tokens per Intelligence Index task, 14% more than Kimi K3 at 48K, while its first-party token prices are 33% lower.

Additional model details:
➤ Context window: 1M tokens.
➤ Size: 2.8T total, 104B active parameters
➤ Input modalities: Text and image
➤ Weights and license: Weights currently not published, Moonshot is expected to release the weights soon after launch
➤ Pricing: $2/$10/$0.20 per 1M input/output/cache hit tokens, 33% lower than Kimi K3 on all three rates.

Congratulations to the team at @Kimi_Moonshot on the release!

selectedTweets.text:
WAIT… Kimi K3.1 Pro became so good at exploiting vulnerabilities that Moonshot had to NERF its hacking capabilities before releasing the weights.

> removed cyber data from training and RL
> exploit success rate went from 90.5% to 81%
> it’s still more than DOUBLE its predecessor’s 33.3%

but they actually plan to INCREASE the cyber capabilities in future models. from the blog: 
“First, we aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability. K3.1 Pro's offensive cyber capability is, by design, below what our pipeline can produce, and remains behind that of frontier proprietary models. Second, we intend to progressively raise the cyber capability available in open weights. We believe making K3.1 Pro available in a non-discriminatory way benefits people who need dual-use capabilities for defensive purposes. When a capable model is open and runs on infrastructure its users control, many more teams gain the means to audit the code they maintain — including legacy systems that rarely receive dedicated security reviews. We believe that letting this capability diffuse gradually — rather than concentrating it in a few proprietary systems — ultimately makes all software more secure.”

selectedTweets.text:
Moonshot is taking a very interesting approach to cyber for its new Kimi 3.1 Pro model.

Instead of adding safety guardrails during post-training, they removed cyber-related data in mid- and post-training. This tries to address the problem of people fine-tuning away the safety guardrails for cyber for the open-weight model.

At the same time, Moonshot still has a more powerful internal version of the model with full cyber capabilities. Now, like the US, China’s true AI frontier is no longer public.
